name: documind-phase-4c-baseline
description: Twenty-five manually labeled questions over the deterministic Phase 4C corpus.

cases.question: How many days of annual leave do full-time employees receive?
cases.referenceAnswer: Full-time employees receive 20 days of paid annual leave per calendar year.

cases.question: How many days per week may employees work remotely?
cases.referenceAnswer: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week.

cases.question: When is an itemized receipt required for a business expense?
cases.referenceAnswer: An itemized receipt is required for every business expense over 25 dollars.

cases.question: Which systems require MFA?
cases.referenceAnswer: MFA is mandatory for email, source control, payroll, and VPN access.

cases.question: How quickly must a severity-one incident be acknowledged?
cases.referenceAnswer: A severity-one incident must be acknowledged within 15 minutes.

cases.question: When must a severity-one postmortem be completed?
cases.referenceAnswer: A severity-one postmortem must be completed within five business days after resolution.

cases.question: How long are customer financial and tax records retained?
cases.referenceAnswer: Customer financial and tax records are retained for seven years.

cases.question: When is the production maintenance window?
cases.referenceAnswer: Planned production maintenance occurs on Tuesdays from 02:00 to 04:00 UTC.

cases.question: What is the yearly vacation allowance?
cases.referenceAnswer: The yearly paid annual leave allowance is 20 days for full-time employees.

cases.question: How often can staff work from home?
cases.referenceAnswer: Employees may work from home up to three days per week.

cases.question: Above what amount is proof of purchase needed for reimbursement?
cases.referenceAnswer: An itemized receipt is required for expenses over 25 dollars.

cases.question: Where is two-factor authentication compulsory?
cases.referenceAnswer: Two-factor authentication is compulsory for email, source control, payroll, and VPN access.

cases.question: What is the reaction time for the highest severity outage?
cases.referenceAnswer: The highest-severity incident must be acknowledged within 15 minutes.

cases.question: How soon must we erase customer information after a verified request?
cases.referenceAnswer: A verified deletion request must be completed within 30 calendar days unless a legal hold applies.

cases.question: What hours are reserved for planned downtime?
cases.referenceAnswer: Planned production downtime is Tuesdays from 02:00 to 04:00 UTC.

cases.question: Which cabin may be booked for a flight lasting more than six hours?
cases.referenceAnswer: Business class may be booked for flights longer than six hours with vice-president approval.

cases.question: Compare retention for security audit logs and customer financial records.
cases.referenceAnswer: Security audit logs are retained for 90 days, while customer financial records are retained for seven years.

cases.question: How frequently are compliance records and production databases backed up?
cases.referenceAnswer: Compliance records are backed up daily, while production databases are backed up every six hours.

cases.question: Describe the escalation routes for incidents and critical support tickets.
cases.referenceAnswer: Incidents page the secondary on-call after ten minutes without acknowledgement and then assign an incident commander. Critical support tickets escalate to the duty manager if unresolved after one hour.

cases.question: Compare receipt rules for ordinary expenses and business travel.
cases.referenceAnswer: Both ordinary and travel expenses require itemized receipts over 25 dollars. Ordinary claims are due within 30 calendar days of purchase; travel claims are due within ten business days after returning.

cases.question: What are the response commitments for severity-one incidents and critical support cases?
cases.referenceAnswer: Severity-one incidents require acknowledgement within 15 minutes, while critical support tickets receive an initial response within 30 minutes.

cases.question: Which policy covers restricted payment credentials and which covers financial record retention?
cases.referenceAnswer: The data-classification policy marks payment credentials as restricted, and the record-retention policy keeps financial records for seven years.
